title: Graduate Customer Intelligence Executive - French Speaking
description:
Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on.

 Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Adanola and Huel use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform — and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin.

  

 About the role 

 The Customer Intelligence team are responsible for ensuring our customers take action on Fospha data: turning data into clear recommendations, guiding marketers through budgeting decisions and helping client teams become experts in the Fospha platform.

 This is the entry point into the function, and it is a hands-on one. You'll work across live customer accounts from the point that they go live with Fospha, becoming the trusted expert in the domain, our customers and the decisions they are making across their marketing mix. It's a role for someone who wants to learn how to turn data into customer action, in a business where these actions are meaningful and exciting.

 
 Team : Customer Intelligence

 Level : Graduate - Entry Level

 Location : London, White City 

 
 What you’ll be doing: 

 
 You'll join our Customer Intelligence Team and work across customer accounts, becoming a trusted expert in the insight, model, and data quality that sit behind them

 You'll be responsible for the customer outcomes your team owns — driving action on insight, trust in the model, and confidence in data quality — contributing to customer retention alongside the Account Manager

 You'll build deep expertise in your specialism and use it to solve real customer problems, turning data into clear recommendations, building trust in our methodology, and keeping data accurate and flowing

 You'll be confident and effective in customer-facing moments relevant to your team, building credibility with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

 You'll be collaborative, working closely with Account Managers and other specialist teams, feeding customer insight back to Product, and keeping everyone aligned with regular progress updates

 
 In addition to your core responsibilities, we expect you to be excited by the opportunity Gen AI brings and find new ways of working utilising our Gen AI hub to increase our efficiency

  

 The Centre of Excellence 

 
 The Centre of Excellence is Fospha's early-careers programme that develops ambitious, high-performing talent through focused training, hands-on experience and cross-functional exposure. Starting in Customer Intelligence, you'll gain foundational experience while being prepared for future opportunities across the organisation. The programme operates on the following principles:

 Individual Responsibility from the Get-go: You will quickly be responsible for the success of your work, able to make an individual impact early in your career

 Work alongside SLT at Leading Businesses: You will be engaging with Senior Leadership and C-Level executives at the leading retail brands, getting exposure to how the top companies operate

 Become a Customer Facing Expert: You will be working directly with customers, often meeting them in person and developing your ability to create strong interpersonal relationships

 Cross-Functional Exposure: we offer unique opportunities to learn from and collaborate with every department in the business — many daily

 Comprehensive Training: In addition to the extensive on-the-job learning opportunities, you'll receive a broad and blended in-person training curriculum covering essential topics such as Business Storytelling, Account Management, Market Research & Product and Financial Management

 Real Mentorship: Regular one-to-ones, feedback, and career conversations with people invested in your progression, not just your output

 Career Development: High performers have clear opportunities to quickly advance their careers at Fospha — whether progressing within our Customer Teams toward strategic and/or management roles or moving into other departments that align with your skills and interests

 Modern Tools: Hands-on exposure to Gen AI tooling through our Gen AI hub, so you're building modern, AI-fluent ways of working rather than legacy processes

 
  

 What we can offer you 

 
 Salary: £34k + discretionary 10% bonus

 A workplace pension ~~through Royal London~~, with Fospha matching your contributions up to 3%

 A £1,000/year flexible benefits allowance to put towards private medical insurance, dental cover, a health cash plan, gym membership, extra holiday, or a pension top-up - whatever suits you!

 Access to Wellhub, giving you one membership across gyms, boutique studios, and wellbeing apps

 25 days' annual leave plus 8 UK bank holidays, an extra day off for your birthday! and more holiday the longer you stay (26 days after 3 years, 27 after 6)

 Life assurance worth 4x your annual salary, from day one

 Cycle to Work scheme, plus discounts on everyday spending through our benefits portal — Apple, Tesco, IKEA, M&S, Deliveroo, cinema tickets and more

 Quarterly one-to-one sessions with a financial adviser, plus access to payroll-deducted loans through Salary Finance

 Paid volunteering days each year

 Regular socials, free weekly snacks, and Lunch & Learn events at our Scale Space office, plus access to the wider Blenheim Chalcot community

 Opportunities to travel — including to our India and North America offices

 
  

 What are we looking for? 

 
 We hire for potential – you don’t need a technical degree or marketing background. We’re looking for:

 Curious, proactive individuals who are keen to learn and grow

 Excellent verbal and written communication skills

 Strong relationship-building ability, both internally and externally

 Analytical mindset, comfortable interpreting data and creating insights – proficiency in Excel!

 Organised and able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously

 Solving problems for customers

 Interest in emerging technologies and excited by the potential and opportunity AI brings

 
  

 Our Values and Principles 

 
 You will be able to demonstrate examples of our core principles:

 Seek inclusion & diversity: We create an environment where everyone feels welcome, and people are encouraged to speak and be hear

 Work Hard, Work Well, Work Together: We take responsibility for making things happen, independently and together; we help colleagues in need and close loops, making sure our work is complete and has lasting impact

 Grow: We are proactive, curious and unafraid of failure

 Customer at the heart: We care about the customer, feel their pain and love building product that solves their biggest problems

 Candour with caring: We deliver candid feedback with kindness and receive it with gratitude

title: Sales Director, EMEA
description:
Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply.  Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic! 

 About Tailscale  

 Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.
 Tailscale is redefining secure networking by making it simple for organizations to securely connect people, devices, and workloads anywhere in the world.

 At Tailscale, we're solving one of the most fundamental challenges in modern infrastructure: secure connectivity. Our product is loved by developers, trusted by IT and security teams, and rapidly expanding within organizations of every size. As adoption accelerates, we are investing in a regional sales motion that matches the scale of our ambition across EMEA.

 We are looking for a founding Sales Director, EMEA to build and lead one of Tailscale's most important growth initiatives. This is a rare opportunity to shape how a category-leading company enters and scales a major region, develops strategic customer and partner relationships, recruits an exceptional team, and creates the operating model for long-term growth.

 About the Role 

 You will be a regional leader, seller, coach, and builder. You will own the EMEA sales strategy and lead teams across multiple customer segments, while personally helping advance the region's most important opportunities and executive relationships.

 You will define regional priorities, territory and segment strategy, hiring plans, outbound and expansion motions, and the operating cadence for the business. You will also help spearhead partnerships across the region, including channel, cloud, technology, and strategic alliance relationships that can accelerate customer acquisition and expansion.

 Initially, you will lead a focused team of Account Executives across multiple segments and work closely with Customer Engineering, RevOps, Marketing, GTM Engineering, and Executive Leadership. As the business grows, you will play a central role in scaling the team, developing frontline leaders, and building the regional organization.

 This UK-based role reports directly to the President and offers the opportunity to build Tailscale’s EMEA sales organization from the ground up.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Build the EMEA Business 

 
 Lead  the current team and build the EMEA sales organization and go-to-market motion.

 Develop the regional strategy, operating model, territory design, account segmentation, and coverage plan across multiple sales segments.

 Set clear regional priorities and translate company goals into executable plans for new business, expansion, and partnerships.

 Establish repeatable playbooks that reflect the needs of customers and markets across the UK and broader EMEA region.

 Provide regional market insight that helps shape company strategy, product priorities, and investment decisions.

 
 Lead From the Front 

 
 Personally support and, when appropriate, lead Tailscale's highest-value and most strategic EMEA opportunities.

 Develop trusted executive relationships with CIOs, CISOs, CTOs, infrastructure leaders, security leaders, and business executives.

 Serve as the regional executive sponsor and quarterback for complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles.

 Coach teams on discovery, qualification, account strategy, executive engagement, negotiation, and deal execution.

 Navigate technical, commercial, legal, procurement, and executive stakeholders to drive successful customer outcomes.

 
 Lead and Scale Multiple Segments 

 
 Lead Account Executives serving multiple customer segments, from commercial and mid-market organizations through enterprise and accounts.

 Create differentiated motions, coverage models, and performance expectations appropriate to each segment.

 Recruit, hire, onboard, and develop exceptional sales talent across the region.

 Build a high-performance culture grounded in accountability, collaboration, curiosity, customer value, and continuous learning.

 Develop future leaders and create the management structure required as the EMEA organization scales.

 
 Build Regional Partnerships 

 
 Help define and execute the EMEA partnership strategy alongside the Partnerships organization and Executive Leadership.

 Identify markets and customer segments where partners can accelerate awareness, pipeline creation, implementation, and expansion.

 Create clear rules of engagement, joint account plans, and co-selling motions with priority partners.

 Represent Tailscale with senior partner executives and at relevant regional customer and industry events.

 
 Create Pipeline and Regional Awareness 

 
 Lead an outbound-first and account-based sales motion across the region.

 Personally build executive relationships within high-priority accounts and partner ecosystems.

 Partner with SDRs, Marketing, GTM Engineering and Partnerships to create qualified pipeline.

 Build scalable account planning, prospecting, event, community, and partner-sourced pipeline programs.

 Ensure the region develops a balanced pipeline across customer segments, products, countries, and sources.

 
 Drive Operational Excellence 

 
 Own regional forecasting, pipeline health, hiring plans, and performance management.

 Establish a rigorous operating cadence across forecast reviews, pipeline creation, deal inspection, account planning, and talent development.

 Use data to identify trends, improve execution, allocate resources, and communicate regional performance to leadership.

 Partner closely with Product and Engineering to provide structured customer and market feedback from EMEA.

 Build the metrics, processes, and cross-functional relationships required to scale the organization effectively.

 
 What We Are Looking For 

 
 An experienced sales leader who has built or materially scaled a high-growth SaaS business in EMEA.

 A proven leader of teams spanning multiple customer segments, with the judgment to adapt the sales motion by segment and market.

 A builder who is comfortable operating with ambiguity, limited infrastructure, and significant ownership.

 A strong seller and coach with a consistent record of winning complex new-business and expansion opportunities.

 Experienced in recruiting, developing, and retaining high-performing Account Executives and sales leaders.

 Demonstrated success building outbound pipeline and establishing repeatable regional go-to-market motions.

 Experienced developing channel, technology, cloud, reseller, or strategic partnership relationships in EMEA.

 Executive presence and credibility with CIOs, CISOs, CTOs, and senior business leaders.

 Strong business acumen and experience navigating complex buying committees, procurement processes, and enterprise sales cycles.

 Deep familiarity with the UK and broader EMEA technology market; additional European language skills are valuable but not required.

 This role is based in London and is hybrid (2-3 days/week in-office) with ability to travel throughout EMEA as needed. #LI-Hybrid 

 
 You'll Thrive Here If You... 

 
 Want to build a region rather than inherit a mature organization.

 Enjoy leading from the front while creating leverage through managers, teams, and partners.

 Can balance strategic planning with hands-on customer and deal leadership.

 Are energized by developing different sales motions for commercial, mid-market, enterprise, and strategic customers.

 See partnerships as a core growth lever rather than a separate or secondary function.

Tailscale's compensation package includes base salary, equity, and comprehensive benefits. The salary range displayed on each job posting represents the target range for a new hire's base salary. Individual offers may vary based on experience and skill set.
 What We Offer 

 
 An inclusive, flexible environment where you can be your authentic self. We recognize the impact of diverse voices and backgrounds on the growth of our people, product, and company. And that flexibility in how and when you work empowers our team to integrate work and life.

 Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.
 The Role 

 We are seeking a Precompute Platform Lead to own and scale Addepar's precompute layer — the platform that pre-calculates financial analytics and transparently integrates precomputed and real-time results, delivering step-change improvements in query latency and concurrency for enterprise-scale wealth management firms.

 The team operates on terabyte-scale datasets, leveraging vector-oriented programming and distributed systems to enable sub-second performance. You will lead the evolution of this capability from targeted use cases to a platform-wide performance layer — solving hard problems in incremental computation, vectorised processing, and distributed data architecture as you scale.

 Applicants must have, and maintain, the right to work in the United Kingdom from the first day of employment. Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

 What You’ll Do 

 
 Own the precompute platform roadmap in partnership with Product and engineering leadership, defining and meeting aggressive performance KPIs for daily processing, incremental processing, and query latency across enterprise clients

 Architect, implement, and maintain engineering solutions to solve sophisticated problems; reduce complexity through the adoption of strategic data architecture and workflows

 Drive integration with core compute infrastructure, growing the share of query traffic served through the precompute layer

 Continue global region support, building a repeatable architecture that scales across Addepar's multi-region deployment

 Drive deeper vectorisation of the calculation layer, moving compute-intensive factor math from row-by-row execution into the columnar engine for step-change throughput improvements

 Improve team efficiency by engaging with operational partners

 Who You Are  

 
 B.S., M.S., or Ph.D. in Mathematics, Statistics, or similar numerate field (or equivalent practical experience).

 Extensive background in software engineering or data platform roles, with significant experience in performance engineering under large scale and high-concurrency systems

 A hands-on engineering leader with demonstrated experience in vector-based data processing

 Experience leading global, distributed engineering teams through production system transformation

 Strong cloud data infrastructure background — AWS, Databricks, Kubernetes

 Cross-team technical influence — demonstrated ability to facilitate constructive discussions around complex technical and organisational issues and drive architectural decisions across team boundaries

 Data-driven prioritisation mindset — you build and act on usage analytics and cost/performance/accuracy tradeoffs, not just receive them

 Finance or wealth management domain knowledge is a plus but not required

 A confident and positive outlook with low ego; high degree of ingenuity, resourcefulness, and problem-solving skills

 Our Values

 Drive Innovation - Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry.

title: Sr. Security Engineer - GRC Fintech & Financial Services EU/UK
education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or in an engineering/STEM field.
description:
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge.  Our team is small, highly motivated, and focused on engineering excellence. This organization is for individuals who appreciate challenging themselves and thrive on curiosity. We operate with a flat organizational structure. All employees are expected to be hands-on and to contribute directly to the company’s mission. Leadership is given to those who show initiative and consistently deliver excellence. Work ethic and strong prioritization skills are important. All employees are expected to have strong communication skills. They should be able to concisely and accurately share knowledge with their teammates. 
 ABOUT THE ROLE: 

 We are seeking an experienced Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Engineer focused on European Union and United Kingdom information security and financial services regulation to help scale compliance for SpaceXAI and xMoney. As we expand deeper into regulated EU/UK markets, maintaining a robust, transparent, and technically sound information security GRC program is critical. You will architect the systems and processes that automate trust — a pragmatic operator who understands that GRC exists to enable the business, balancing rigorous standards with the velocity of a high-growth company. The ideal candidate brings hands-on experience with frameworks such as DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2, and related EU/UK information security and operational resilience obligations, plus GRC engineering skills: Compliance-as-Code, continuous evidence collection, and deep partnership with engineering so controls are designed into the platform rather than bolted on after the fact.

 This role may also include additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to support the team and evolving business priorities. This position may require occasional travel. 

 RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 
 Own and evolve EU/UK financial services and digital operational resilience posture across DORA (including ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing, and third-party ICT provider oversight), and complementary expectations from EBA/ESMA/EIOPA guidance, PSD2/PSR where applicable, and UK PRA/FCA operational resilience requirements supporting xMoney.

 Build and maintain Compliance-as-Code capabilities — policy-as-code, automated control validation, continuous evidence collection, and monitoring integrated into CI/CD — so audit and supervisory readiness scales with the business rather than depending on manual, point-in-time checks.

 Operate and extend GRC platforms (e.g., Vanta) as the backbone for control mapping, evidence management, and continuous compliance; integrate with cloud, identity, logging, and engineering systems to reduce administrative bottlenecks.

 Partner with Architects and Engineering Leads to bake EU/UK information security and regulatory requirements into design early; translate complex obligations into concrete technical implementations and auditor- or supervisor-ready narratives without slowing development.

 Design, implement, and validate technical information security controls relevant to regulated EU/UK environments (access control, logging and monitoring, encryption, change management, vulnerability management, ICT third-party oversight, and secure SDLC) — not just document them.

 Operate the cybersecurity and compliance risk register — identify, quantify, and track risks, distinguishing theoretical gaps from meaningful business and regulatory risk under EU/UK supervisory expectations.

 Lead information security risk assessments and compliance reviews for new products, features, vendors, and architectural changes that affect the EU/UK regulated attack surface, including ICT third-party / critical provider diligence aligned to DORA.

 Liaise with the Data Privacy team on security-relevant intersections (e.g., security measures supporting confidentiality and integrity.

 Own and cultivate relationships with external auditors, assessors, and (where applicable) supervisory contacts on information security topics; serve as the bridge between external parties and internal teams so requests are reasonable, clear, and relevant to our stack.

 Develop, maintain, and continuously improve information security policies, standards, and procedures aligned to DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2 where in scope, and complementary frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2) where they overlap.

 Champion pragmatic governance — prioritize issues that represent real security or business risk over checkbox compliance.

 
 BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

 
 Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or in an engineering/STEM field.

 8+ years of experience in GRC, information security compliance, or technology audit roles in fintech, banking, payments, or other heavily regulated environments with EU and/or UK exposure.

 Hands-on experience implementing or operating controls against several of the following: DORA, the EU AI Act, NIS2, PSD2/PSR, or UK PRA/FCA operational resilience expectations — not only reading the requirements.

 Familiar with data privacy regulations applicable to the EU/UK region (e.g., EU GDPR, UK GDPR, UK Data Protection Act 2018) sufficient to liaise with Privacy counterparts.

 Experience with Compliance-as-Code practices and GRC automation tooling (e.g., Vanta, or similar), with a bias toward continuous monitoring and reducing manual evidence collection.

 Technical fluency sufficient to speak the language of engineering, On-premises, hybrid, or cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure), and security architecture, and to anticipate how design decisions impact information security risk and compliance.

 
 PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

 
 10+ years of information security compliance, GRC engineering, or technology audit-related experience in fintech or financial services with a primary EU/UK focus.

 Hands-on experience implementing technical controls (e.g., IAM, logging and monitoring, encryption, network segmentation, infrastructure hardening) and integrating compliance checks into CI/CD pipelines.

 Experience supporting ISO 27001 and/or SOC 2 programs alongside EU/UK regulatory obligations.

 Familiar with GDPR concepts that commonly intersect with information security (e.g., security of processing, breach notification timelines, encryption/pseudonymization as security measures) when collaborating with DPO/Legal/Privacy functions.

 Familiarity with DORA ICT third-party risk, register of information, threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) concepts, and major ICT-related incident reporting expectations.

 Experience with AI governance under the EU AI Act or related national guidance, especially security controls for AI features in regulated financial products.

description:
About Artificial 
 Help shape the future of specialty insurance At Artificial, we’re building the next generation of technology for the specialty (re)insurance market. Our mission is to transform how brokers and carriers operate in complex markets by removing operational barriers and enabling smarter, faster decision-making.
 We use modern technology to solve real challenges for some of the world’s leading brokers and insurers. By automating the repetitive and structuring the complex, we help our partners unlock new opportunities for innovation and growth.
 You’ll be joining a collaborative team that values curiosity, ownership, and continuous learning. We work in an environment where ideas are heard, support is built-in, and outcomes matter. Everyone here has the chance to make a tangible impact on our products, our customers, and the industry.
 We've just raised $45M (£33M) in Series B funding from lead investor CommerzVentures, new investor Move Capital, as well as all existing shareholders. This investment round gives us the room to grow with confidence, continue to innovate, and ensure that Artificial remains the first choice for brokers and carriers seeking a smarter way to trade digitally.
 Join us, and take the chance to be a part of something that will change the landscape of insurance for generations.
 About the Role 
 We are looking for a Quality Engineer to own test automation across Artificial's product platform. This is a hands-on technical role: we already have a substantial automated test suite - roughly 680 Playwright tests alone, plus extensive backend coverage - but it's grown quickly without a dedicated owner, and needs real structure, consolidation, and meaningful metrics built on top of it. You'll start on Platform, bringing structure to what exists and establishing standards for what gets added next, then extend automation into Transform/customer-configuration testing over time - an area with no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers, in work that's highly specific to each client.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Reorganisation and consolidation: Bring coverage, completeness, and integrity to our existing ~680-test Playwright suite (plus extensive backend coverage) - identifying and removing duplication, fixing or removing flaky tests, and establishing clear structure and naming conventions where the suite has outgrown its original organisation

 Meaningful metrics: Build real, trustworthy metrics off the back of the existing suite - coverage mapped to actual product routes and features (today's closest proxy, Playwright page objects, doesn't map cleanly to routes), pass/fail trends over time, and flaky-test tracking

 Ongoing addition and maintenance: Own the suite as a living asset, not a one-off clean-up - adding new automated coverage as features ship, maintaining existing tests as the product changes, and keeping the suite healthy on an ongoing basis

 CI pipeline scaling: The suite has grown 40% in three months (470 to 680 tests) and is now regularly hitting CI resource limits, with an 8-shard stress-test job approaching a 4-hour timeout. Work collaboratively with the QA Lead and Engineering on a real scaling plan for our existing CI pipeline (Buildkite) - this can't just mean adding more runners indefinitely. You'll be closely involved in shaping this, with full ownership expected to grow over time

 Clarifying automation boundaries: Work with Engineering and FDE teams to establish a clear, documented relationship between platform-level automated tests and FDE "golden tests," removing current ambiguity about what covers what; also align with the performance testing work already underway so load/performance results sit in the same reporting picture rather than a separate silo

 Mentorship: Support QA Engineers with automation as they need it - helping them write and troubleshoot tests, sharing what you know, and building their confidence over time

 Reporting integration: Work with the QA Lead to integrate automated test results into the wider test management approach, so a test failure automatically generates a structured bug report linked back to Linear, rather than issues being created manually on an ad-hoc basis as they are today

 Cross-team collaboration: Work closely with Engineering (who currently own significant existing automation) to agree a clear, documented handover and ongoing collaboration model, avoiding duplicated effort or unclear ownership

 Building Transform/config automation from scratch: Once Platform is on a solid footing, extend automated coverage into FDE/customer-configuration testing - an area that has no automated coverage today, only manual execution by our existing testers. Unlike the Platform work above, this genuinely starts with nothing, in an area that's highly specific to each client rather than standard across the platform

 About You

 Deep experience with Playwright, Cypress, or Selenium, including framework design and CI/CD integration

 Comfortable working in or around a codebase - reading and reasoning about application code, even if not writing production features yourself

 Experience diagnosing and resolving flaky or unreliable automated tests, and designing tests to avoid these problems from the start

 Experience establishing test coverage visibility/reporting from scratch, where none previously existed - you'll use this directly when the role extends into Transform/config automation, which genuinely starts with nothing today

 A methodical, standards-driven approach - you think about frameworks and patterns, not just individual test cases

description:
Hi 👋 I’m Dom Allgood, Client Education Manager at hyperexponential. I joined four years ago as a Curriculum Developer and have spent the last couple of years growing Client Education into the (soon to be) five-person team it is today. Before hx I spent a decade teaching Computing in secondary schools. Outside of work most of my time goes to my two children, and what's left to running and, more recently, mountain biking - where I'm still very much a beginner.
 Client Education exists to get our customers to value as quickly as possible, and to keep them there. We run instructor-led training, own hx Academy where all our self-paced learning content lives, own the certification programme, and run some of our customer events. We've also recently taken ownership of Developer+, and that's where this role comes in. Our first customers are working through the programme now, and as it grows it will need to evolve based on what we learn from them.
 This isn't a typical Delivery Engineer role, you'll sit in Client Education rather than Delivery Engineering. You'll still work closely with the wider Delivery Engineering team, but your day to day is the customers on Developer+: delivering workshops, running drop-ins, reviewing their code, and shaping the programme around what you learn doing it. You'll partner with Product too, so customers can adopt new enhancements quickly and smoothly. There's no established playbook for this yet, so what matters most is the drive to build one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to own, I'd love to hear from you.
 
 About hyperexponential (hx)
 At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes — whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
 Until now, insurance has been making billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision — helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
 Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally — already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
 What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do — from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
 What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
 If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.
 
 About the Delivery Engineering team 
 The hyperexponential Delivery Engineering team is a unique blend of engineers, actuaries, mathematicians and data scientists. We don’t take on traditional “transformations” (we have brilliant partners for that) – we specialise in handling only the most difficult and interesting problems our customers face, where only a combination of technical depth, market expertise and hx knowledge will do.
 The Delivery Engineering team are the experts' experts of the hx platform, knowing it top-to-bottom, inside-out – both breadth and depth. You’ll learn its limits and which can be pushed. You’ll uncover every trick in the book, the secret combinations, and the shortcuts. You’ll combine all of this with a growing knowledge of insurance technology to present 'the art of the possible' to our customers and help shape cutting-edge tech, while working alongside some of the brightest, most ambitious people in the tech and insurance industries.
 
 What you'll be doing
 Move customer teams from hx-led build to independent delivery, shifting effort from pairing toward review and advisory.

 Keep every engagement moving to its prescribed path, sequencing services to each customer's build stage.

 Deliver structured enablement sessions — architecture, coding best practice, testing and deployment, model lifecycles — pitched at each team's level.

 Run code review as a consistent, standards-anchored service, evolving hx's model development standards where reviews expose gaps.

 Provide drop-in support shaped by each customer's build stage, resolving most issues in session rather than escalating.

 Make Developer+ repeatable rather than personality-dependent, documenting delivery and using AI to scale capacity.

 Convert delivery knowledge into hx Academy content, prioritised by what reviews and drop-ins actually surface.

 Act as the technical voice of the customer into Product, feeding back recurring friction on a regular rhythm.

 
 What you'll need to have done
 Built deep hx platform expertise and production-grade Python, including testing, deployment and model lifecycles.

 Have excellent pricing and modelling judgement when working with customer’s - working with insurance & actuarial teams is a plus.

 Developed strong technical enablement instincts, pitching sessions and documentation at the audience's real level.

 Coached customer teams to work independently rather than solving problems for them.

 Operated with high ownership and self-direction, building repeatable process where none exists.

 Prioritised transparently across competing delivery, review and content demands.

 Communicated with credibility and clarity across developers, actuaries, delivery partners and internal stakeholders.

 
 You're unlikely to thrive here if
 You prefer following detailed instructions rather than experimenting and finding your own approach.

 You are uncomfortable working directly with non-technical stakeholders to understand their challenges.

 You avoid tackling ambiguous or open-ended problems where the solution isn't obvious.

 If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.
 
 Compensation
 At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process - our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations - and we're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.
 Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.
 Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.
 
 Benefits
 £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development.
 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total).
 Company pension scheme via Penfold.
 Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life .
 Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno.
 Private healthcare insurance through AXA.
 Income protection and Life Insurance.
 Cycle to Work Scheme.
 
 Additional perks
 Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.).
 Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and game nights.
 Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.
 Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

 Take-home Python challenge followed by Skills Interview

 Our commitment to Diversity
 hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.
 Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.
 If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.
 
 Next steps

Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space.  We are looking for a senior Systems Software Engineer to join our Runtime Software team at Oxford Ionics / IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for working directly with the experimental scientists to implement the real-time control system behaviours and provide abstractions they require for their experiments, contributing to the team’s mission of enabling our science teams to experiment and improve the primitive operations which allow compute, and building towards fault tolerant computation.

 You’ll play an important part in shaping the core, Rust, libraries and the execution environment which take our system from a collection of hardware to a quantum computer, and support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems.

  

 Responsibilities :

 In this position, you will work on developing abstractions over real-time control hardware, supporting the effective delivery of a control system capable of repeatedly and reproducibly driving our ions with nano-second level precision, with abstractions which are conducive to both fast iteration and system scaling.

 You’ll have the opportunity to accelerate the science core to the development of our systems, and contribute to the core execution model of our quantum computers, contributing directly to the success of building utility-scale quantum computers.

 Key responsibilities include: 

 
 Collaborating with scientists to understand their requirements

 Interfacing with system orchestration, non-realtime control and compiler teams to ensure our work integrates seamlessly with the wider software architecture.

 Interfacing with FPGA and electronics teams to shape the overall system architecture.

 Implementing drivers for various real-time devices.

 Producing tooling to enable users of our code to iterate rapidly and fearlessly.

 Developing the execution environment for the user programs which run on our systems.

 Continually evaluating the shape of our APIs and improving them for our internal users.

 
 Requirements: 

 To be successful, you will need strong programming skills in a systems programming language, experience with software system design, and a desire to produce high quality code appropriate to a real-time environment. We’re looking for someone who can quickly iterate on low-level code in a collaborative, cross-disciplinary, environment and contribute effectively within a fast moving, highly technical team.

 
 Have strong programming skills in one or more mainstream programming languages

 Have experience with a systems programming programming

 Have experience with real-time linux or embedded systems or another low-latency computing environment

 Have an interest in or experience with Rust

 Have developed excellent communication skills both within the context of software and across disciplines

 Are comfortable working with rapidly evolving requirements

 Have a desire to maximise impact through quick iteration and short cycles of learning and improvement

Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

Founding Product Designer (UX/UI & Research) 
 London (Hybrid) | Full-time | £70 - £85K + early-team equity
 The role 
 We’re a well-funded startup building category-defining AI for architecture, engineering and construction: an archaic industry at a critical juncture. The Building Safety Act now requires firms to evidence their design decisions, and directors carry personal liability.
 Join Bite as our first in-house designer working strategically and directly with the head of product, founders and engineering team, you’ll own the entire design function and lead the transformation of our beta into a high-quality user experience that shapes the future of Bite’s AI for the built environment.
 
 Why join Bite 
 The problem is genuinely hard. When a structural engineer changes a component in their building design model, the same component exists in drawings, schedules, specs and emails under different names, in different formats, some of which LLMs don’t understand, and with no shared identifier. Detecting these changes, predicting the downstream impacts and propagating them using AI under the engineer's supervision is the core of our product.
 You'll own the UX/UI for the whole product, not a slice of it. There's no design team to inherit and no feature factory to work around. You set the direction, the patterns and the quality bar, and you'll prototype, test and ship rapidly with a small team that can pivot, fast.
 Your work ships to people who pay. The beta is in production with signed customers that include some of the UK's leading structural engineering firms who are keen to build with us. With our tight feedback loops, you’ll have plenty of data to help drive your design decisions.
 
 What we're building 
 Structural engineers work across numerous, fragmented sets of tools with no shared source of truth. When a design changes, propagating that change across files is manual, slow and error-prone, and the errors are expensive.
 Bite is the change management and audit trail layer for structural engineering. The platform does three things that today take weeks of manual work: natural-language search across a project's entire file ecosystem, cross-file impact detection e.g. "I changed Column C7 in the structural model - what drawings, schedules, and specs are now out of date?" and propagation of those changes to every affected file.

description:
Meet Siena 
 Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.
 It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on. 
 The team 
 We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.
 We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.
 If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.
 The Role
 You own the commercial relationship for Siena's highest-value brands: renewals, expansion, executive trust, and knowing your accounts better than anyone. A deployment strategist owns product outcomes for the same accounts, and together you're the Siena pod.
 You're accountable for net dollar retention, expansion quota attainment, and executive relationship health across your book. You own our Growth and Strategic segment accounts, not the full customer book, working at the intersection of customer, sales, and your deployment strategist. Expect moderate travel for in-person workshops, account visits, and QBRs.
 What You'll Do
 Own the commercial relationship end to end for a portfolio of Growth and Strategic accounts, from post-onboarding through long-term growth: build concrete account plans, track impact with data, and hold customers and internal teams accountable when progress stalls

 Map every account and build executive trust: maintain a living stakeholder map, build relationships with decision-makers beyond day-to-day contacts, and own the executive cadence so leadership sees Siena's value before renewal conversations start

 Drive commercial outcomes: own renewal negotiations, independently identify and close expansion opportunities, and quantify customer ROI in cost savings, efficiency, or revenue impact

 Lead cross-functional execution: turn vague customer problems into clear problem statements and execution plans, partnering with other teams as needed

 Who You Are

 Hands-on AI experience: you've built an agent, automated a workflow, or created a tool, not just used ChatGPT for email

 Enterprise experience: managed complex orgs, sold to multiple stakeholders

 Close collaboration experience with product and engineering teams

 Self-directed: brings solutions, not just problems

 Balances empathy with commercial impact, willing to challenge the status quo when it blocks results

 Not a Fit If:

 Why Siena?

 AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.
